findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences an absent destination calendar
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when an event has no destination calendar, but this condition immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. This replaces the previous optional-chain-safe check, so creating any Google Meet event without a configured destination calendar throws a TypeError before calendar/video creation can proceed.

findings.title: Non-Google collective host events are still created against the first host calendar
findings.body: The loop creates one event per destination and supplies `destination.externalId` only to the CalendarManager result metadata. CalendarManager passes only `credential.id` to the provider, while the Office365, Lark, and CalDAV `createEvent` implementations ignore that argument and select `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. Consequently, when a collective event has multiple destination calendars, creation using a later host's credential targets the first host's calendar (or fails due to lacking access), while the stored reference claims the later host calendar. Subsequent updates/deletes will then address the wrong event/calendar.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference for every host
findings.body: For each calendar reference, the recurring-cancellation branch iterates every calendar credential but selects `updBooking.references.find(...)`, which always returns only the first calendar reference. With multiple host calendar references, it repeatedly tries to delete that first event using unrelated credentials and never processes the remaining references. This leaves recurring events on some host calendars and can issue deletion attempts against the wrong account.

findings.title: Google Meet description patch no longer uses the primary-calendar fallback
findings.body: Insertion falls back to `calendarId: "primary"` when no matching destination calendar is found, but the follow-up patch uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is undefined in that case. Google requires a calendar ID for `events.patch`, so events created in the primary fallback path can fail the asynchronous patch and retain an incomplete description/hangout-link information.

findings.title: Organization slug persistence condition was inverted
findings.body: The organization `slug` is now persisted only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true, whereas the prior behavior persisted it when that feature was disabled. This makes newly created organizations lack a slug in non-team-billing deployments and assigns an active slug in the mode that previously retained it only as `metadata.requestedSlug`, changing organization routing/verification behavior unrelated to destination calendars.
